explanations.explanation: True, baker. The LORD says, “Has not My hand made all these things? And so they came into being…” (Isaiah 66:2). I make cookies one stamp at a time and my mustache gets tired. He made everything, and the question shows it. It comes right after He asks what kind of house you could build for Him.

Not quite, friend. The LORD really does say it: “Has not My hand made all these things? And so they came into being…” (Isaiah 66:2). It comes right after His question about building Him a house. He is the One who made it all, so He is the One who made the heaven and earth He just talked about.

explanations.answer: The humble one who trembles at His word
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The LORD says, “This is the one I will esteem: he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word.” (Isaiah 66:2). Notice He doesn't say the one with the biggest anything. I think that's good news for all of us.

explanations.answer: The one who brings the grandest offerings
explanations.explanation: Not this one, friend. The LORD names the one He will esteem, and it's “he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word.” (Isaiah 66:2). Offerings come up in the very next verse, but they aren't what He points to here. He looks at a person who is humble and listens to His word.

explanations.answer: The one with the most famous name
explanations.explanation: Close, but no cookie. The text doesn't say the LORD esteems a famous name. He says He will esteem “he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word.” (Isaiah 66:2). That's the one He points to, and fame isn't part of that description.

explanations.answer: They have chosen their own ways
explanations.explanation: Right, baker. Look at what verse 3 does: “Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who slays a man…” The offerings are right there, and the LORD still sets them beside awful things. Then He says what is going on: “Indeed, they have chosen their own ways and delighted in their abominations.” (Isaiah 66:3). So the problem isn't that they brought something. It's that they did it their own way and not His.

That's not what the text says, friend. Nobody in these verses is told the offering is too small. The LORD says, “Indeed, they have chosen their own ways and delighted in their abominations.” (Isaiah 66:3). The trouble He names is about the ways they chose.

explanations.answer: They offer on the wrong days
explanations.explanation: Days never come up here, baker. The text doesn't mention a single calendar. What the LORD says is, “Indeed, they have chosen their own ways and delighted in their abominations.” (Isaiah 66:3). That's the line to hold onto.
Yes, baker. The LORD says, “So I will choose their punishment and I will bring terror upon them…” (Isaiah 66:4). They chose their ways, and now He chooses their punishment. This is a heavy verse.

I know that word sounds friendlier, friend, but it isn't what the text says. The LORD says, “So I will choose their punishment and I will bring terror upon them…” (Isaiah 66:4). Right before it, He said they chose their own ways and delighted in their abominations. This is a heavy verse, and the word is punishment.

Teachers aren't in this verse, baker. I do love a good teacher, but the text says, “So I will choose their punishment and I will bring terror upon them…” (Isaiah 66:4). The blank is punishment. It's a heavy verse, so we take it plainly.

explanations.answer: He called and no one answered
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says, “…because I called and no one answered, I spoke and no one listened.” (Isaiah 66:4). His reason isn't a missed rule. It's that He spoke and nobody paid Him any mind. I think this part is heavy. Then the verse says what they did instead: “But they did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.”

Feast days don't show up in this verse, friend. The reason the LORD gives is, “…because I called and no one answered, I spoke and no one listened.” (Isaiah 66:4). He called and spoke, and nobody answered or listened. Then it adds that they did evil in His sight.

explanations.answer: They moved to a far country
explanations.explanation: Nobody packs a bag in this verse, baker. The LORD gives His reason: “…because I called and no one answered, I spoke and no one listened.” (Isaiah 66:4). Nothing here says they went anywhere. It says they didn't answer and didn't listen.

Yes, baker. The text says, “Your brothers who hate you and exclude you because of My name…” (Isaiah 66:5). It's said to those who tremble at His word. I think that has to sting, being shut out by your own brothers. The LORD sees it, though, and speaks to them directly.

The text doesn't say that, friend. It says, “Your brothers who hate you and exclude you because of My name…” (Isaiah 66:5). It does call them brothers, but the reason given is the LORD's name. No quarrel is mentioned, so I won't invent one.
No city-leaving here, baker. The LORD says, “Your brothers who hate you and exclude you because of My name…” (Isaiah 66:5). The reason is His name. The text never says these people left anywhere.

explanations.answer: They will be put to shame
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The brothers say, “Let the LORD be glorified that we may see your joy!” and the LORD answers, “But they will be put to shame.” (Isaiah 66:5). It's a short sentence with a lot of weight in it. The ones who tremble at His word hear this straight from Him.

Not in this verse, friend. After the brothers say, “Let the LORD be glorified that we may see your joy!” the LORD says, “But they will be put to shame.” (Isaiah 66:5). That is what He says will happen to them. Being proven right isn't what the verse says.

explanations.answer: They will be left in peace
explanations.explanation: Not in this verse, baker. After the brothers speak, the LORD says, “But they will be put to shame.” (Isaiah 66:5). That's the only outcome He names for them here. Peace isn't mentioned for these brothers.

Watchmen are a good guess, but the text names someone else, friend. It says, “It is the voice of the LORD, repaying His enemies what they deserve!” (Isaiah 66:6). The voice from the temple is the LORD's. No watchman is mentioned in the verse.

False is right, baker. The verse says the voice from the temple is “…the voice of the LORD, repaying His enemies what they deserve!” (Isaiah 66:6). No watchmen are named. The voice belongs to the LORD Himself.

Not quite, friend. The LORD asks, “Who has heard of such as this? Who has seen such things?” (Isaiah 66:8). Those questions show how astonishing this birth is. It isn't pictured as something people hear about all the time.

Right, baker. He asks, “Who has heard of such as this? Who has seen such things?” (Isaiah 66:8). The questions show how astonishing this is, not something people hear about all the time. If I told you my cookies baked themselves before the oven warmed up, you'd ask the same thing.

That's the one, baker. The verse says, “Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.” (Isaiah 66:8). The picture is of Zion as a mother. She gives birth to her children, and it happens as soon as she is in labor.

Babylon isn't named in these verses, friend. The text says, “Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.” (Isaiah 66:8). Zion is the mother in this picture. Stay with the name the text gives.

Nineveh isn't in this passage, baker. The LORD names the mother in the same verse: “Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.” (Isaiah 66:8). It's Zion. In this picture she's the one in labor, and she gives birth to her children as soon as it starts.

explanations.answer: He will make it wait longer
explanations.explanation: That's not where the question points, friend. The LORD asks, “Shall I bring a baby to the point of birth and not deliver it?” (Isaiah 66:9). A question like that is meant to be answered no. He brings it to the point of birth and He delivers it.

The question isn't undecided, baker. The LORD asks, “Shall I bring a baby to the point of birth and not deliver it?” and adds, “Or will I who deliver close the womb?” (Isaiah 66:9). He's the One who delivers, so those questions answer themselves. He doesn't leave it hanging.

True, baker. The verse says, “Rejoice greatly with her, all who mourn over her…” (Isaiah 66:10). So the call isn't only for those who are already happy. Those who mourn over her are told to rejoice too.

It's actually true, friend. The text says, “Rejoice greatly with her, all who mourn over her…” (Isaiah 66:10). Those who mourn over Jerusalem are included in the call. It goes out to everyone who loves her and everyone who mourns over her.

explanations.answer: They are carried on her arm
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The LORD says, “you will nurse and be carried on her arm, and bounced upon her knees.” (Isaiah 66:12). It's a picture of little ones being held close. I'll admit, nobody ever carried me on an arm. I got slid into a drawer.

explanations.answer: They are sent off to her fields
explanations.explanation: Fields aren't mentioned here, friend. The LORD says, “you will nurse and be carried on her arm, and bounced upon her knees.” (Isaiah 66:12). It's a close, held-in-arms picture. Nobody gets sent away in it.

explanations.answer: They are left outside her gates
explanations.explanation: The picture goes the opposite way, baker. The LORD says, “you will nurse and be carried on her arm, and bounced upon her knees.” (Isaiah 66:12). These little ones are held close, not left outside. No gates come up in the verse.

It's true, friend. The LORD says, “As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you, and you will be consoled over Jerusalem.” (Isaiah 66:13). He uses the picture of a mother and her son. It's the LORD Himself who says He will comfort them.
Yes, baker. The verse says, “When you see, you will rejoice, and you will flourish like grass…” (Isaiah 66:14). Not a tall tree, just grass. I think grass is a nice everyday picture.

A cedar sounds grand, friend, but it isn't in this verse. The text says, “When you see, you will rejoice, and you will flourish like grass…” (Isaiah 66:14). The comparison in the verse is grass, not a cedar.

No olive trees in this verse, baker. The text says, “When you see, you will rejoice, and you will flourish like grass…” (Isaiah 66:14). Grass is the comparison the verse uses. It's a simple one, and it fits.
